summary: Independent acceptance confirms all ten reported discrepancies. Problem P3 is Major because a false expansion occurs in the supplied proof of the central kernel identity and its downstream Bailey-tree use is explicit. The finite repair is demonstrated; the kernel and main conclusions are not disproved. Nine other findings remain Minor because the exact surviving arguments and local scopes are identified. Cited prior-kernel equivalences remain unverified from complete retained sources.

problems.title: Wrong prefactor modulus in the tau=-1 reduced identity

source_claim.claim: The prefactor is (q^(2k+2);q^(2k+2))_infinity^2 although theta has modulus3k+2.

assumptions: mu_0=infinity and mu_k=0 as explicitly supplied

counterexample.calculation: LHS=(q;q)_infinity^-1 sum_n>=0 q^(n*n)/(q;q)_n; coefficients through q4 are[1,2,4,7,13]. PrintedRHS[1,2,4,7,11].
counterexample.proof: Only n=0,1,2 can contribute throughq4; direct multiplication of finite coefficient lists proves discrepancy2q4.

counterevidence: General Macdonald product(5.16) uses matching modulus.
problems.impact: False displayed special case; no counterexample to mainTheorem1.2.

correction.boundary: Restores the intended reduced product; full main identity assessed separately.
correction.verification_status: Direct proof or exact calculation supplied in current report and named notes

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The admitted k=1,a=1,b=0,tau=-1 and stated mu_0=infinity convention reduce the left side to (q;q)_infinity^(-1) sum q^(n^2)/(q;q)_n. Only n=0,1,2 contribute through q^4; multiplication yields [1,2,4,7,13], whereas the printed modulus-4 prefactor gives [1,2,4,7,11].
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The main (1.5) and general product use K=3k+tau+3, hence modulus 5 in this test.
independent_verification.repair_check: Replace 2k+2 by 3k+2 in the reduced prefactor. This local special-case failure does not refute the main identity.

problems.title: Missing factor and incorrect exponent in the kernel proof expansion

source_claim.claim: Double sum omits1/(wq;q)_m and uses binom(r-s,2)+r².

counterexample.calculation: First printed2 versuscorrect20/7; second printed71/15 versuscorrect24/5 even when missingfactor=1.
counterexample.proof: Expand(q^-r)_s and(q^-m)_s; signs cancel and argument(wq^(m+1))^s yields exponentr²-rs+s² and remainingprefactor1/(wq)_m. Explicittermsn2m0 are8/3,2,1/15 printed versus8/3,2,2/15 corrected.

counterevidence: The correct preceding transformed 2phi1 expression and the succeeding 1phi1 expression agree after the independently derived finite Pochhammer expansion is substituted.

The source p.16 explicitly cites [8, Theorem 4.3], [89, Theorem 5.1] and [31, Corollary 7.9]. Their complete sources are not retained in this packet; precise equivalence has not been independently verified, so the citations are not counted as an established alternative proof.
Finite checks of the kernel support the theorem; such checks do not make the false printed equality valid.
problems.impact: The printed finite double-sum equality fails under admissible nonnegative indices and nonsingular parameters. It is part of the supplied proof of the central reproducing identity (4.5), subsequently used in the constant/u/uv coefficient proof of Theorem 4.4 and shifted Bailey-tree iteration on p.19. This is a Major failure of the supplied core proof, not a disproof of the identity or principal results.

correction.statement: Restore the factor 1/(wq;q)_m and replace the exponent by r^2-r*s+s^2; use the resulting finite expansion before shifting r to r+s.
correction.boundary: The finite Pochhammer identities directly prove this local algebraic repair, under the manuscript's reciprocal-factorial convention and nonzero denominators. No arbitrary-parameter convergence argument or equivalence with external prior theorems is claimed.
correction.verification_status: Independently re-derived finite expansion and admissible rational witnesses; actual downstream use checked on source pp.16-19.

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The double sum on p.17 omits 1/(wq;q)_m and gives an incorrect exponent. At q=1/2,z=2/3,w=3/5, n=0,m=1 yields printed 2 versus 20/7; n=2,m=0 separately isolates the exponent error, 71/15 versus 24/5. All denominators are nonzero and indices satisfy the theorem. Expanding (q^-r;q)_s and (q^-m;q)_s cancels the signs and yields exponent r^2-r*s+s^2 and the missing prefactor.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The corrected finite expansion gives the next printed 1phi1 line after the index shift. Source p.16 explicitly cites prior [8, Theorem 4.3], [89, Theorem 5.1], [31, Corollary 7.9], but no complete retained source was available for verifying their precise equivalence. These citations and finite checks support the identity without validating the false printed equality. Source p.19 actually uses (4.5) for the constant/u/uv coefficients in Theorem 4.4 and the shifted iteration.
independent_verification.repair_check: Substitute the corrected finite Pochhammer expansion before shifting the index. This proves the local repair under the source conventions. The supplied central proof remains defective and warrants Major; the reproducing identity and main product conclusions are not claimed false.

Direct inequalities instead yield ceil(k/2)<=a'<=k-1, 0<b'<=a', and 0<=b''<=a''<=k-2.

problems.title: Missing square in the explicit modulus-seven product

correction.verification_status: Direct proof or exact calculation supplied in current report and named notes

independent_verification.independent_reasoning: The p.32 modulus-seven example lacks one (q^7;q^7)_infinity factor. The exact left coefficients through degree 10 are [1,2,6,11,23,41,75,126,213,343,551]; the single-factor product gives [1,2,6,11,23,41,75,127,215,349,562]. The numerator is split into E1=r^2-r*s+s^2-r+s and E2=r^2-r*s+s^2+r; the quadratic lower bounds justify the finite r,s<=12 cutoff, including negative 2r-s cases.
independent_verification.counterevidence_checked: The corrected squared factor agrees through the exact checked range and follows from the already-stated rank-two normalization. The isolated example is not needed for the general below-the-line argument.
independent_verification.repair_check: Square the prefactor. No universal theorem is certified solely from the finite coefficient test.
